theorems.name: Brockian.AdmissibilityHLCriterion.Admissible
theorems.ledger_run: roadmap #11 — Hardy-Littlewood admissibility criterion; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: The genuine global HL criterion: Admissible H (covers no full residue system) iff for every prime p, nu_p(H) < p; equivalently image.card < p. Includes the finiteness reduction (suffices p <= |H|) and connections to the q-nu count (admissible iff count>0). Examples {0,2} admissible, {0,2,4} inadmissible (decide COMPUTATION). NOT claimed: HL conjecture (infinitude), density/asymptotics.

theorems.name: Brockian.ErdosStraus.ErdosStraus
theorems.ledger_run: open-territory swarm; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: OPEN-TERRITORY partial results toward the Erdos-Straus conjecture (open since 1948; 4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z in positive integers). Swarm-built, AXLE @4.32, axiom-clean. UNCONDITIONALLY PROVED: the even case, the divisible-by-3 case, the multiplicativity reduction erdosStraus_of_dvd (inherited by multiples), erdosStraus_of_prime_case (the whole conjecture REDUCES TO PRIMES), and residue classes n=3 mod 4 and n=2 mod 3, via explicit verified Egyptian-fraction identities. The full conjecture ErdosStrausConjecture is a DEFINITION (unproven statement), NOT a theorem -- deliberately. Open frontier: primes in the hard residues p = 1,121,169,289,361,529 mod 840. This is an honest formalized contribution to an open problem, resolving all but a density-zero set of n; it does NOT claim to solve the conjecture.

UNCONDITIONALLY PROVED: the even case, the divisible-by-3 case, the multiplicativity reduction erdosStraus_of_dvd (inherited by multiples), erdosStraus_of_prime_case (the whole conjecture REDUCES TO PRIMES), and residue classes n=3 mod 4 and n=2 mod 3, via explicit verified Egyptian-fraction identities. The full conjecture ErdosStrausConjecture is a DEFINITION (unproven statement), NOT a theorem -- deliberately. Open frontier: primes in the hard residues p = 1,121,169,289,361,529 mod 840. This is an honest formalized contribution to an open problem, resolving all but a density-zero set of n; it does NOT claim to solve the conjecture.

theorems.name: Brockian.ErdosStrausResidues.erdosStraus_covered
theorems.ledger_run: open-territory loop; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: Extended Erdos-Straus coverage + sharpened open frontier (open-territory loop, AXLE @4.32, axiom-clean). Adds verified divisibility identities 5|n (witnesses 2m,4m,20m) and 7|n (2m,15m,210m); erdosStraus_covered (n even/div3/=3mod4/=2mod3 all decomposable) and its contrapositive erdosStraus_open_reduces (any counterexample is odd, coprime to 3, =1 mod 4). SHARPENED: erdosStraus_open_reduces_mod12 (counterexample => n=1 mod 12) and erdosStraus_open_frontier_mod24 (n%24 in {1,13}). HONEST finding: a computational search over many moduli found NO linear parametric family closing the frontier subclasses n=1,13 mod 24 -- matching the known theory that these feed the genuinely-open hard primes p=1,121,169,289,361,529 mod 840. The boundary is drawn, not crossed.

theorems.provenance_note: Unified Galois n-gon classification (swarm capstone, AXLE @4.32, axiom-clean): TFAE for n>=3 that the real cyclotomic field Q(2cos 2pi/n) is quadratic <=> n in {5,8,10,12} <=> Euler totient phi(n)=4 (routes through quadratic_iff_totient_four + totient_eq_four_iff). Four concrete minimal-polynomial witnesses identify WHICH quadratic: n=5 -> X^2+X-1 (phi-1), n=10 -> X^2-X-1 (phi), n=8 -> X^2-2 (sqrt2), n=12 -> X^2-3 (sqrt3). The Golden Galois Dichotomy: among the four, discriminant=5 (the golden field) exactly for n in {5,10}, separating golden from silver(8)/bronze(12). Field-equality not attempted (documented).

theorems.name: Brockian.GoldbachSelectionRule.admissibleUnits
theorems.ledger_run: harvest (Chris's Affine Selection Rules paper) — unified dihedral selection rule; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: THE UNIFICATION (paper Thm 2.5): for any perm f of ZMod m, |admissibleUnits f| = m-1 if f 0 = 0 else m-2 (admissibleUnits_card, general prime m, real reasoning: univ minus {0, f^-1 0}, coincide iff f 0 = 0); admissible_card_dihedral across the affine group Sigma = D_m. Gap law (translation) and Goldbach law (reflection) proved to be its two restrictions (gap_pairs_eq_translation_admissible / goldbach_pairs_eq_reflection_admissible); m=5 concrete tables by decide. Rmk 2.6: phi(m)-[f0!=0]. Reuses AffineSymmetry/Admissibility/AdmissibilityDiagonal, no dup. The 4/3 asymptotic (Thm 3.1) is NOT claimed (conditional-on-HL, documented). Goldbach untouched.

theorems.name: Brockian.GoldenDivisibility.golden_in_cycleSpectrum_iff_five_dvd
theorems.ledger_run: swarm capstone; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: The Golden Divisibility Law: for every n>=1, phi-1 is an adjacency eigenvalue of the cycle C_n IFF 5 divides n (full iff, both directions). Generalizes the prime uniqueness theorem golden_unique_to_five (5|p forces p=5) to ALL cycles: the pentagon n=5 is the smallest, every fifth cycle inherits the golden mode. Forward reuses the cos_eq_cos_iff -> 5k=n(5m+-1) -> 5|n chain (no primality); backward uses the k=j witness at n=5j. Corollary golden_unique_to_five_recovered specializes back to the prime case. AXLE @4.32, axiom-clean.

theorems.name: Brockian.GoldenSpectralCharacterization.golden_quadratic_roots
theorems.ledger_run: swarm/Harmonic; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: Spectral fingerprint of the golden ratio (swarm-built, AXLE @4.32, axiom-clean): the root set of the golden quadratic X^2+X-1 equals exactly {phi-1, -phi}, and both are adjacency eigenvalues of the 5-cycle -- so the pentagon's two non-Perron eigenvalues ARE the golden quadratic's roots. golden_quadratic_roots (root characterization), golden_roots_mem_pentagon_spectrum (both in spec C5), golden_ratio_spectral_characterization (capstone set-equality), golden_roots_sign_split (phi>1 pins the pair by sign).

theorems.name: Brockian.LehmerTotient.Lehmer
theorems.ledger_run: open-territory loop; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: OPEN-TERRITORY necessary conditions on a counterexample to Lehmer's totient problem (open since 1932: does phi(n)|n-1 imply n prime?). Open-territory loop, AXLE @4.32, axiom-clean. A Lehmer number = composite n with phi(n)|(n-1). PROVED: any such n is ODD (lehmer_odd; phi even vs n-1 odd), SQUAREFREE (lehmer_squarefree, flagship; p^2|n => p|phi(n)|n-1 while p|n), and has >=3 distinct prime factors (lehmer_three_primes; the p*q case reduces to ab|(a+b) with a,b>=2 a!=b, impossible). Existence is NEVER asserted or denied.

PROVED: any such n is ODD (lehmer_odd; phi even vs n-1 odd), SQUAREFREE (lehmer_squarefree, flagship; p^2|n => p|phi(n)|n-1 while p|n), and has >=3 distinct prime factors (lehmer_three_primes; the p*q case reduces to ab|(a+b) with a,b>=2 a!=b, impossible). Existence is NEVER asserted or denied.

theorems.name: Brockian.OddPerfectConstraints.OddPerfect
theorems.ledger_run: open-territory loop; AXLE @4.32
theorems.provenance_note: OPEN-TERRITORY necessary conditions for odd perfect numbers (open ~2000 years; existence unknown). Open-territory loop, AXLE @4.32, axiom-clean. FLAGSHIP oddPerfect_not_square: an odd perfect number cannot be a perfect square (sigma of an odd square is odd, but Perfect means sigma n = 2n even -> contradiction). Plus oddPerfect_not_prime_pow (not a prime power) and sanity conditions (positive, odd, >1). All theorems are IF-an-odd-perfect-number-exists-THEN necessary conditions; existence is NEVER asserted or denied. Euler's form p^k*m^2 was the stretch and honestly dropped (not proved).
